title: Preference for Physical Buttons and Knobs
summary: Reviews in this topic center on customers wanting physical controls instead of touchscreen interactions for commonly used functions such as climate, seat, and convenience features.

positive.summary: One positive review specifically praises the physical-button idea by highlighting problems caused by closely spaced touch controls for memory settings.

negative.summary: Negative reviews say touchscreen-based controls are harder, more distracting, and less safe than physical buttons for frequent adjustments.

undetermined.summary: Undetermined reviews mostly express a preference for physical buttons, knobs, or tactile controls for climate, seat, and other quick-access functions without enough context to classify the sentiment more specifically.

limitations: Most sampled fragments are classified as undetermined, which limits how specifically the overall sentiment balance can be interpreted.
This cluster spans several different controls and features, including climate, seat functions, distance adjustment, memory settings, and door controls, so it is not a single narrowly defined issue.
Only selected fragments were provided, so examples are insufficient to describe all negative cases in detail.
